The question asks if routine laboratory markers are useful for differentiating between non-alcoholic and alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH). The relevant match from the dataset is: "Differentiation of nonalcoholic from alcoholic steatohepatitis: are routine laboratory markers useful?".

This completion states that, according to the evidence from the healthcare Q&A matches, higher MCVs (Mean Corpuscular Volume) and AST/ALT ratios in ASH do not differentiate NASH (Non-Alcoholic Steatohepatitis) from ASH (Alcoholic Steatohepatitis). Instead, these biomarkers might be useful for guiding patients with NASH for liver biopsy and selecting therapy.

In other words, routine laboratory markers are not highly effective for differentiating between the two conditions, but they could potentially guide certain decisions or suggest further testing.
